title: REQ-20261113-OPS005 — Death certificate summary (BDM Victoria, died 12 Oct 2026) & claimant identity checks (Mei Chen; Robert & Lily Chen)
content:
Summary of the certified death certificate and claimant identity documents for case REQ-20261113-OPS005 (specimens — demo only).

Death certificate: issued by the Victorian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages (BDM Victoria). Deceased: Mei Chen, female, DOB 05/06/1945, aged 81. Date of death: 12 Oct 2026. Place of death: Box Hill Hospital, Box Hill VIC. Usual residence: Box Hill VIC. Cause of death: natural causes (cardiac failure). Informant: Robert Chen (son). Registration number masked (ending 1187); registered 26 Oct 2026. Copy certified as a true copy by a Justice of the Peace on 10 Nov 2026.

Matching: name, date of birth and suburb match the Caldova member record for CP-3019042 ✅.

Document authenticity (Content Understanding, reviewed by Financial Crime): GENUINE ✅ — layout, registry seal, registration-number format and certification stamp are consistent; no editing artefacts; dates are internally consistent (registration after the date of death, certification after registration).

Claimant identity:
• Robert Chen — Victorian driver licence, DOB 30/01/1974, certified copy: GENUINE ✅; name and DOB match the nominee on Mei's binding nomination.
• Lily Chen — Australian passport, DOB 11/05/1977, certified copy: GENUINE ✅; name and DOB match the nominee on Mei's binding nomination.
• Bank accounts — each held in the claimant's own name ✅.

Financial crime screen: no indicators. There were no changes to Mei's contact or bank details in the months before her death, the claimants' details match the nomination records, and PEP and sanctions screening of both claimants returned no match. Risk: LOW — the payment can proceed once Benefits & Eligibility complete their assessment and the Team Leader approves the death benefit.

Handling note: this is a bereavement case. Any contact must be gentle, explain why each step is needed, and avoid asking the family for the same document twice.
